title: Decision (ADR)
description: One entry of DECISIONS.md: a heading 'ADR-NNNN: title' or 'D-NNN — title' at any level, normalized from its '**Field:** value' lines (CONTRACTS.md, Normalization), or, for a decision log written in prose, from its heading and paragraphs (form: prose). Immutable once accepted; corrected by a superseding decision.

form.description: prose: a decision-log entry with no Status line (1.3.0). Its decision is its Decision paragraph or else its text, and its status is what its own words say: superseded when its heading or a line says 'superseded by <id>', else accepted. Absent: the ADR form, whose fields are required.

status.description: The first word of the Status line, lowercased.

superseded_by.description: ADR ids named after 'superseded' in the Status line (whole or in part).

context.description: '**Context:**' — the forces at play (the Nygard form). Stands in for why when an ADR has no Why line.

options.description: '**Options considered:**' bullets: the alternatives, each with why it lost.

door.description: '**Door:** one-way|two-way'. A one-way door needs a reversal trigger anyway: what would make it worth the cost.

reversal_trigger.description: The '**Reversed when:**' line: the measurable condition that reopens the decision.

satisfies.description: '**Satisfies:** epic/NFR-1, epic/REQ-3' — the requirements this decision exists for.

extra.description: '**Label:**' lines the parser does not map, keyed by label.

placeholders.description: Fields the parser found holding a template token (TODO(domain), <…>). Reported as warnings, not errors.

allOf.description: The ADR form names its status line and consequences; a prose entry has neither.
An ADR says why: a Why line, or a Context line (the Nygard form). A prose entry says it in its text.
A date is required unless the template still holds its placeholder (TODO(domain)), which bootstrap fills. A prose entry is dated by its commit.
A superseded decision names its successor.
A one-way door still names what would reopen it.
